help.list: the machines in your library: system, state, vCPUs, memory, disk used, graphics
help.start: start it as the Machines app does: in its window, or without one
help.open: open its window on the desktop
help.stop: shut it down, as its system's power button does
help.poweroff: turn it off at once, like pulling the plug
help.pause: pause it, or let it go on
help.suspend: save it to disk and turn it off; the next start goes on from there
help.snapshot: list, take, go back to or delete its snapshots
help.clone: a copy of it beside it (--duplicate: the same identity, its snapshots too)
help.rename: give it a new name; while it's off, its folder and transfer folder take the name too
help.set: change its settings, as Configure does (sizes such as 8G or 512M)
help.name: NAME is a machine's name (any case; its start is enough when only one matches), its id or its folder.
help.exit: Exit status: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 wrong command, 3 not running, 4 no such machine, 5 needs your LordOS session.
label.name: Name
empty: No machines in {library} yet. The Machines app makes them.
noMachine: There's no machine called “{name}”. “machines list” shows them.
ambiguous: “{name}” could be more than one machine: {list}
unknown: Not a command or option of machines: {arg}. “machines help” shows them.
badOption: {option} isn't an option here, or it needs a value.
missing: Something is missing: {what}. “machines help” shows how.
noLordVm: Machines isn't installed on this computer.
noSession: This needs your LordOS desktop session, and it isn't running.
needsSession: {name} needs an administrator step before it starts ({why}): start it while your LordOS session is running.
needsWindow: Its window needs your LordOS desktop session. “machines start {name} --no-window” starts it without one.
noSuspendGpu: A machine with a graphics card can't be suspended; shut it down instead.
renamedFolder: “{old}” is now called “{name}”; its folder is {dir}.
renamedLater: “{old}” is now called “{name}”. It's running, so its folder keeps its name: once it's off, “machines rename "{name}" "{name}"” names it “{folder}”.
folderWhenOff: {name} is running, so its folder keeps its name: run this again once it's off to name it “{folder}”.
renameNothing: {name} already has that name, and its folder too.
badNewName: A name is 1 to 64 bytes of text and doesn't start with a dot.
folderTaken: The Machines folder already has “{folder}.lordvm”: pick another name.
transferTaken: Machines/Transfer already has a folder called “{folder}”: pick another name.
folderKept: The name is saved, but its folder keeps its old name: {why}
badName: A machine's name is 1 to 64 bytes of text.
notInLibrary: That machine isn't in your Machines library.
busy: {name} is starting or shutting down; try again in a moment.
startedNoWindow: {name} is running without a window. “machines open {name}” shows it.
stillStarting: {name} is still starting; its window shows how it goes.
groupStarted: {name} is running: its gateway first, then its workstation.
groupStopped: {name} is off: its workstation first, then its gateway.
groupDamaged: {name} is damaged: one of its machines is missing or isn't its own.
groupNameTaken: There’s already a group or machine called “{name}”.
groupFolderTaken: The Machines folder already has “{folder}”: pick another name.
gatewayFailed: {name}'s gateway didn't start ({why}), so its workstation wasn't started.
workstationFailed: {name}'s workstation didn't start ({why}); its gateway is still running.
help.fresh: a machine group back to its verified image with a new identity: the workstation, and the gateway too with --gateway (Tor's entry guards go with it); the group must be off
help.member: one machine of a group: --member gateway alone; --member workstation starts the gateway first
freshRunning: {name} is running: shut the group down first.
freshNeedsYes: Start Fresh throws away the workstation's changes: add --yes to do it without a question.
freshAsk: Start {name} fresh? The workstation's changes, files and snapshots go; the gateway stays as it is. [y/N]
freshAskBoth: Start {name} fresh, gateway too? Both machines' changes go, and Tor picks new entry guards. [y/N]
freshDone: {name}'s workstation is fresh: its verified image, a new identity.
freshDoneBoth: {name} is fresh: both machines are back to their verified image, with a new identity.
freshNotGroup: {name} isn't a machine group: Start Fresh is for groups.
help.exec: run a program in a Linux machine as its signed-in person; its output, and its exit status as ours (125: it couldn't run). Needs automation on in Configure
help.cp: copy a file into a machine or out of it; one side is NAME:PATH (~ is the person's home folder there)
help.logs: the guest's journal, its serial console (--serial) or the machine's own log (--machine); --follow keeps reading
help.console: the machine's serial console in this terminal; Ctrl+] leaves
help.shell: a shell as the person signed in to the machine, through its LordOS tools; Ctrl+] leaves
help.mcp: a local MCP server on standard input and output, for a coding agent: it acts only on machines with automation on
help.apply: make or change a machine from a short text file (name, memory, cpus, disk, network, iso, ports, shares)
help.import: bring in a machine of another virtualization app (a .vmx, .vbox, .utm, .pvm, .ova or a disk) with its identity, as the app's Migrate does
noAutomation: Automation is off for {name}: turn it on in its Configure.
outputCut: The output was longer than what comes back: only its start is shown.
timedOut: The program in {name} ran out of time and was stopped.
cpOnlyFiles: Only files can be copied: {path} isn't one.
cpOneSide: Say which side is the machine: one of the two is NAME:PATH, the other a file on this computer.
cpOutside: {path} isn't among your files, or it is protected.
noLog: There's no such log for {name} yet.
consoleHint: The serial console of {name}. Ctrl+] leaves.
applyAskShares: {file} asks {name} for these, which reach beyond the machine: {list}. Allow them? [y/N]
applyNoShares: Nothing was changed: what reaches beyond the machine wasn't allowed (it asks on a terminal only).
applyRunning: {name} is running: shut it down to change it from a file.
overBudget: {name} didn't start: it needs {need} MB and {free} MB are left for machines. Suspend or shut down another machine, or give it less memory.
